title: Half-Height Double-Row CFET Standard Cells for Area Optimized Placement in A7 CMOS Node
problem: Double-Row CFET architecture enables cell track height scaling but introduces limitations on standard cell layout design and block-level area optimization.
motivation: Achieve significant area scaling in advanced CFET technology nodes through optimized standard cell design and placement strategies.
method: Half-Height Double-Row CFET (stacked transistors in compact rows) lets designers freely adjust standard cell layouts and then optimize cell placement during the final routing stage of chip design. This two-stage approach—flexible cell design followed by block-level optimization—achieves better space efficiency than fixed designs. The technique stays within realistic manufacturing limits for the metal interconnection layers.
key_novelty: First half-height stacked-transistor design enabling area optimization at both cell and block levels of chip design.
contributions: 50% area reduction on standard cell layouts
10% block-level area scaling on ARM Cortex-M0 32-bit core at 90% utilization
14% projected block-level scaling with enriched standard cell library
High flexibility in standard cell layout design

metrics.area: 50% cell area reduction, 10% block area scaling, 14% projected scaling
metrics.other: Track height scaling via shared middle row vias

limitations: Evaluated on A7 CFET technology; specific to CFET device architecture.
primary_theme: Half-height double-row CFET design for area scaling
